Issue #4043:
first of all, congratulations on the new release! this is an amazing codebase and framework <3

flask's 1.x.x setup.py lists semvers that might cause breaking changes:

https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/1.1.x/setup.py#L57-L59
https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/1.0.x/setup.py#L53-L56

specifically, with the new releases of itsdangerous and MarkupSafe, it's possible here to unintentionally increase the versions of those packages while remaining on a 1.x.x version of flask. for example I saw this error occur in a service i manage:

reproduction: take a currently running flask application's python environment, pip freeze. make a new venv, and install, pip freeze, check out the diff


flask shouldn't upgrade major versions of these dependencies to avoid breaking changes. i realize that better package management like poetry would help with this, but hindsight is 2020 :)

Environment:

- Python version: 3.6
- Flask version: 1.x.x


PR title:
set maximum versions for 1.1.x to avoid new major versions

PR body:
Our *strong* advice to all maintainers of applications experiencing issues with upgrades is to pin dependencies using a tool such as [pip-compile](https://pypi.org/project/pip-tools/). Issues can happen with any transitive dependencies in your stack, not only Flask's, so applications need to pin to control when they get updates.

In this *specific* case, because we intend the 2.0, etc. releases to be a new baseline and are immediately not supporting the 1.1.x line, we will make a new release to set maximum versions. We do not intend to do this in general for future releases.

fixes #4043

{
  "path": "tests/test_dependency_versions.py",
  "content": "import subprocess
import sys

def test_maximum_versions():
    result = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "show", "flask"],
        capture_output=True, text=True
    )
    requires_line = [l for l in result.stdout.splitlines() if l.startswith("Requires:")]
    assert len(requires_line) == 1
    requires = requires_line[0].split(":", 1)[1].strip()
    deps = {}
    for dep in requires.split(", "):
        name, _, version = dep.partition(" ")
        deps[name] = version
    for name in ["Werkzeug", "Jinja2", "itsdangerous", "click"]:
        assert name in deps, f"{name} not in dependencies"
        assert "<" in deps[name], f"{name} does not have an upper bound"
        assert deps[name].count(",") == 1, f"{name} does not have both lower and upper bounds"
        parts = deps[name].split(", ")
        assert len(parts) == 2, f"{name} does not have two version constraints"
        lower = parts[0].strip()
        upper = parts[1].strip()
        assert lower.startswith(">="), f"{name} lower bound should be >="
        assert upper.startswith("<"), f"{name} upper bound should be <"
        lower_ver = lower[2:]
        upper_ver = upper[1:]
        assert lower_ver < upper_ver, f"{name} lower version {lower_ver} is not less than upper version {upper_ver}""
}
